svg.title: Four Checks Before Buying a Cleaning Franchise
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-franchise-due-diligence-roadmap; chapter number: 12; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Four Checks Before Buying a Cleaning Franchise; subtitle: The contract, not the mop, is the business; caption: Ex-franchisees and a franchisor founder describe fees stacking to 20-35% of billing, sometimes 40%, finder fees at 4x monthly value, and real pay near $7 an hour.; assumptions note: Week ordering is an editorial sequence of the testified checks; no practitioner set durations for them.; note: Sources Mike Mak (6MDrTK46_8g at 00:04:31 and 00:06:32); Commercial Cleaning CEO (xqw9zag57Uk at 00:05:18); Clean For A Dream (fs86ZhCBfJ8 at 00:30:23 and 00:56:29); AJ SIMMONS (Bbay8f0-XFM at 00:03:28).; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Interrogate the fee stack; deliverable: Written answers on support fees and what each new account costs; gate: Royalty near 10%, marketing 2-10% and admin 5-10% totaled against 20-35% drag; week: Week 2; title: Check reputation; deliverable: Complaint search, Ripoff Report check, tenured and exited franchisee interviews; gate: Buying in is like getting married; unresolved complaints stop the deal; week: Week 3; title: Convert the package into hours; deliverable: Post-fee payout divided by $16-$30 an hour versus about 100 hours worked; gate: A $705 payout on about 100 hours is roughly $7 an hour; week: Week 4; title: Confirm contract ownership; deliverable: Answer on whether the franchise can reassign happy accounts; gate: If accounts can be reassigned, walk away from a glorified-employee role
